items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was hitting the scales at 170 pounds and looking almost as round as Jimmy Rushing.

ctx.x: room and board for Lily and myself. As a beggar, I couldn't be a chooser. I had a good paying gig in Brittany in a place called Douarnenez the 16th and 17th of July. Lily had taken a train to Royan from Paris and met me when I arrived the afternoon of the 18th. The name of the place where Jean was working was "Cafe de l'Hotel de Ville". It was a brasserie-restaurant and was owned by two very nice people Marcelle and Charles. They had a terrace in front, where we played. We immediately attracted a lot of people…

Lily remained in Royan and I came back after the festival of Complain-la-Tour. People had been missing me and had been screaming my name in the street in front of the Cafe de l'Hotel de Ville. We liked the place, having plenty of good food and drinks. I weighed 150 pounds until I went to this place. When I left there I was hitting the scales at 170 pounds and looking almost as round as Jimmy Rushing. And Lily was almost looking like Ella Fitzgerald.

Although Lily and I were salty at Madame Calvé because of the deal she pulled on me, we started to be happy about the way it turned out because I started getting more and more gigs that paid me twice as much for one night that what I was making in her place in one week. So the matter of the fact is that she really did us a favor. And the rest of the year finished with me doing concerts and galas, here there and everywhere in Europe.
